{{2012–13 Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball standings}}

The '''2012–13 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Arizona]] during the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]].  They were led by fourth-year head coach [[Sean Miller]] and played their home games at [[McKale Center]] in [[Tucson, Arizona]] as members of the [[Pac-12 Conference]].

Seeded 6th in the West Region of the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2013 NCAA tournament]], the team defeated (11) [[2012–13 Belmont Bruins men's basketball team|Belmont]] and (14) [[2012–13 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team|Harvard]] by a combined score of 40 points before losing 73–70 to (2) [[2012-13 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship#Sweet Sixteen|Sweet Sixteen]].<ref name="season-stats">{{cite web |url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/ariz/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2012-13/stats/season_stats_final.pdf |title=2012‐13 University of Arizona Basketball Season Stats |publisher=The University of Arizona – Official Athletics Website |date=March 29, 2013 |access-date=March 30, 2013 |archive-date=January 27, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130127012348/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/ariz/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2012-13/stats/season_stats_final.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

After starting the season undefeated in non-conference play, the team went 12–6 in conference and fell to [[2012–13 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]] in the [[2013 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]] semifinals. The team's mid-season record of 14–0 was the second best start in program history since the 1931–32 team opened the season 16–0.<ref>{{cite news |title=No. 3 Arizona holds on for 60-57 win over Utah |last=Marshall |first=John |publisher=Associated Press |url=http://hosted2.ap.org/CARIE/a4cb5a6027c04c8690df451653b3b750/Article_2013-01-05-T25-Utah-Arizona/id-5e3d9901ce8347a0b77d0208201673bf |date=January 5, 2013}}</ref>

Arizona entered the season ranked 11th in the [[Coaches' Poll|Coaches]] and 12th in the [[AP Poll|AP]] preseason polls,<ref>{{cite web |title=2013 NCAA Men's Basketball Rankings – Preseason (Nov. 5) |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/rankings/_/year/2013/week/1/seasontype/2 |publisher=[[ESPN.com]] |access-date=8 January 2013}}</ref> climbed to 3rd in both after going undefeated into January,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/rankings/_/year/2013/week/9/seasontype/2 |title=2013 NCAA Men's Basketball Rankings – Week 9 (Dec. 31) |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |publisher=[[ESPN.com]] |access-date=8 January 2013}}</ref> and then fell to 20th (Coaches) and 21st (AP) just prior to the start of the NCAA tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/rankings/_/year/2013/week/1/seasontype/3 |title=2013 NCAA Men's Basketball Rankings – Postseason (Mar. 18) |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |publisher=[[ESPN.com]] |access-date=8 January 2013}}</ref>

Before the season began Sean Miller and his staff recruited the nation's 3rd-ranked class of 2012<ref name="pascoe_01">{{cite news |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce|title=UCLA leapfrogs Arizona in recruiting class rankings |url=http://azstarnet.com/sports/blogs/pascoe/ucla-leapfrogs-arizona-in-recruiting-class-rankings/article_05b30f04-8f30-11e1-8260-0019bb2963f4.html |date=April 25, 2012 |newspaper=[[Arizona Daily Star]]}}</ref> and brought in three well-regarded transfers,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://tucsoncitizen.com/wildaboutazcats/2012/05/07/lyons-transfer-to-arizona-assures-highly-competitive-practices-with-mcconnell/ |title=Lyons’ transfer to Arizona assures highly competitive practices with McConnell |newspaper=[[Tucson Citizen]] |first=Javier |last=Morales |date=May 7, 2012 |access-date=October 26, 2012 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130204210414/http://tucsoncitizen.com/wildaboutazcats/2012/05/07/lyons-transfer-to-arizona-assures-highly-competitive-practices-with-mcconnell/ |archive-date=February 4, 2013 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> among them starting point guard Mark Lyons, who led the team in scoring with 15.6 points-per-game, including 24.3 points-per-game in NCAA tournament play.<ref name="season-stats"/>

==Preseason==

===Summer Exhibition Tour===
Practices began earlier than otherwise allowed by the NCAA in preparation for a six-day foreign tour to the [[Bahamas]] in August.  (NCAA rules allow teams to conduct 10 practices in preparation for a foreign tour.)  Although NCAA rules allow for foreign tours once every four years, the Bahamas tour was Arizona's first since 2006.  It was the seventh in program history.  The team won its games 136–66 and 99–57.<ref name="pascoe_02">{{cite news |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |title=Bahamas game secondary in value for Wildcats|date=August 12, 2012| newspaper=[[Arizona Daily Star]]| url=http://azstarnet.com/sports/blogs/pascoe/bahamas-game-secondary-in-value-for-wildcats/article_ec07890e-e4a2-11e1-aec1-0019bb2963f4.html |access-date=August 25, 2012}}</ref>

===Red-Blue Game===
Arizona's annual pre-season Red-Blue scrimmage took place at McKale Center on October 21, selling out for the second-straight season.<ref>{{cite news |author=Marshall, John |title=Wildcats impressive at annual scrimmage |publisher=Associated Press |url=http://bigstory.ap.org/article/wildcats-impressive-annual-scrimmage |date=October 21, 2012}}</ref>  A half-time ceremony celebrated the 25-year anniversary of the [[1987-88 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|1987-88 basketball team]], the first in program history to reach the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship#Final Four|Final Four]].  The team's 35 victories remain the most in school history.  Members of the team present included Tucson-native [[Sean Elliott]], Arizona's all-time leading scorer, with 2,555 career points;<ref name="UA-records">{{cite web |title = 2012-13 Arizona Men's Basketball Media Guide |publisher = Arizona Intercollegiate Athletics |url = http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/ariz/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2012-13/misc_non_event/2012-13_MBKB_Guide.pdf |year = 2012 |access-date = March 26, 2013 |page = 52 |archive-date = February 26, 2013 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130226005533/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/ariz/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2012-13/misc_non_event/2012-13_MBKB_Guide.pdf |url-status = dead }}</ref> [[Steve Kerr]], whose 57.8% three-point field-goal percentage in the 1987–88 season is the best in NCAA history (with a minimum of 100 shots made);<ref>{{cite web | title = 2011-12 NCAA Men's Basketball Division I Records | publisher = National Collegiate Athletic Association | url = http://fs.ncaa.org/Docs/stats/m_basketball_RB/2012/DI.pdf | year=2012 | access-date = January 9, 2013}}</ref> and [[Anthony Cook (basketball)|Anthony Cook]], who recorded a program-best 278 career blocked-shots.<ref name="UA-records"/>
